$comment: H1 (v0). Every field this widget captures and every breadcrumb source it will ever install, each carrying the release it ships in. The design makes the claim this file answers: 'Nothing is captured that is not listed in of this document; the list is also shipped as a machine-readable manifest.' A claim a client cannot check is a claim they have to take on trust, and this product's whole argument is that they should not have to. tools/verify-capture.mjs asserts it against the BUILT artefacts, in both directions: nothing emitted is missing here, and nothing tagged v0.1+ is reachable from the v0 build.
$releaseComment: What THIS build ships, and the axis every `release` tag below is read against. It was implicit — `tools/verify-capture.mjs` hard-coded "v0" — so the moment M2 shipped breadcrumbs, screenshots and masking, the checker reported its own product as a leak: six findings, every one of them the tool being a release behind. A stage that is written down moves in one edit and is visible in the artefact a client reads.

context.$comment: The CaptureContext. A CLOSED type: validates 'no extra keys and no null values', which is only enforceable because it is closed. The omission convention is that an unavailable field is an ABSENT KEY — never null, never an empty string — so `optional: true` here means 'may not appear', not 'may be empty'.

fields.typeOnlyBecause: The key exists on CaptureInput and report.ts forwards it when non-empty, but nothing at v0.1 ever populates it — the 8 KB custom cap that sheds categories is v1. So it is visible to the type-reading check in direction 2 and absent from every payload. Marked rather than silenced: a checker that quietly covers less than it appears to is worse than one that covers less and says so.

fields.what: The REVIEWED SITE's build metadata — never our server's commit.
Host metadata via setMetadata/addMetadata, plus the reserved `cr.` prefix.

breadcrumbSources.$comment: The table, every row. ALL v0.1 — the release table is explicit that v0 ships 'no breadcrumbs … no monkey-patching of any host global' and that 'capture's stub footprint in v0 is 0 bytes'. They are listed here at v0 precisely because the interesting assertion is their ABSENCE: verify-capture greps the built artefacts for each installer and fails if one appears.

sources.records: message, redacted filename, lineno, colno, error.name, first 10 stack frames
reduced reason; an Error becomes {name, message, stack}

sources.installs: wraps console.error and console.warn via the patch registry

sources.records: method, redacted URL, status, ok, type, redirected, duration_ms, aborted — never bodies, headers, FormData or credentials
method, redacted URL, status, duration_ms — never responseText, response, responseXML, the request body or headers

sources.installs: SUBSCRIBES to the onNav event — 04 installs no navigation patch of its own
sources.unverifiableBecause: 04 installs no navigation patch at all — it subscribes to the onNav event. There is nothing of ours to grep for, and the own history patch is sanctioned by A3 and ships at v0 for route detection.

sources.installs: a throttled click listener, max one breadcrumb per 100 ms
sources.records: a selector string; the element reference dies with the handler frame
sources.unverifiableBecause: Indistinguishable from our own work in the shipped bytes: The capture net adds a click listener for hit-testing, so a grep for one proves nothing. The v0 promise this source falls under is checked positively instead — see hostGlobals below, and the release table: 'no monkey-patching of any host global'.

neverCaptured.$comment: The table, which is v0 and has CI tests of its own. Listed here so the manifest is the single machine-readable answer to 'what does this thing take', including the negative half — the half a client actually worries about.
items: Any input[type=password] — value, placeholder, or autofill state
[contenteditable] text content, and innerText/innerHTML/textContent of any element as breadcrumb data
localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB and Cache Storage contents — except the widget's own snag: keys
document.cookie — never read, including our own snag_off/snag_on
The review-link token (snag_k) and the bearer session
Request bodies — fetch init body, xhr.send(body), FormData
All request and response headers, not merely auth headers
Keyboard events of any kind — keydown, keyup, keypress, input, beforeinput, paste
navigator.credentials, navigator.geolocation, navigator.mediaDevices — never called, no exceptions (D25)
Framework hydration payloads — __NEXT_DATA__ beyond buildId, __remixContext, __sveltekit_*, Apollo/Redux state

hostGlobals.$comment: The release table for v0: 'no monkey-patching of any host global. Capture's stub footprint in v0 is 0 bytes.' This is the POSITIVE form of the breadcrumb absence check and the one a client can run themselves — every source above that is unverifiable by its own installer is covered by this, because every one of them would have to wrap something here.
